  "raw_idea": "Multi‑hop question answering often relies on reasoning over a chain of facts in a knowledge graph, yet current language‑model training typically uses isolated head‑relation‑tail triples, depriving the model of the surrounding context that supports multi‑step inference. We propose to enrich each target triple (or path) with additional triples drawn from the same source passage, forming a local context subgraph that is presented together with the primary supervision signal. The model will be fine‑tuned under two regimes: one using only the target triple/path and another that also incorporates the supporting context. To improve the reliability of the base facts, we will introduce an adaptive repair loop that detects one‑hop failures, generates corrective examples, and iteratively refines the model. After this cleaning stage, we will apply reinforcement‑learning‑based optimization on lower‑hop QA instances and evaluate transfer to deeper multi‑hop queries.",

input.problem: Large language models (LLMs) trained for knowledge-graph (KG) question answering are typically supervised on isolated head-relation-tail triples. Such supervision omits the surrounding passage/source context in which the triple occurs, and this omission is hypothesized to limit the model's ability to perform multi-step (multi-hop) inference over a chain of facts. A second, related problem is the unreliability of the base facts themselves: noisy or unresolved one-hop facts propagate and compound as reasoning chains get deeper.
input.target_domain: Knowledge-graph multi-hop question answering (KGQA/KBQA) with LLM supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning; KG construction from text (disease-specific KGs).
input.target_system: Open-weight instruction-tuned LLM (e.g., Qwen3-14B class) fine-tuned on KG-derived question-answer items over KGs extracted from source text (e.g., GraphMERT-extracted Gastroparesis/Diabetes KGs).
input.proposed_method: Context-augmented supervised fine-tuning of an LLM: for each primary target KG triple (or reasoning path), attach additional triples extracted from the same source text chunk to form a local context graph (CG). Two supervision regimes are compared: (a) KG-grounded supervision, using only the target triple/path; (b) CG-grounded supervision, using the target triple/path plus supporting context triples. On top of this, an adaptive repair loop detects unresolved one-hop failures with an LLM judge, generates targeted corrective examples, iteratively fine-tunes on them, and quarantines/removes problematic noisy triples. Finally, reinforcement-learning optimization is applied using lower-hop QA items, and generalization is measured on deeper (3-hop, 4-hop, 5-hop) queries.
input.hypothesis: H1 (context): CG-grounded supervision yields higher multi-hop QA accuracy than KG-grounded supervision at fixed backbone, data, and training budget. H2 (repair): the adaptive repair loop raises retained one-hop accuracy and, by strengthening the lower-hop factual foundation, improves deeper-hop performance. H3 (RL transfer): RL on lower-hop QA items initialized from repaired SFT checkpoints produces larger and more stable gains on 3-5-hop queries than RL initialized from unrepaired checkpoints or SFT alone. H4 (conditional): the benefit of context augmentation increases with hop depth (larger at 4-5 hop than at 1-2 hop).
input.research_question: Under a fixed LLM backbone, training data, and compute budget, does augmenting each target KG triple/path with same-passage supporting triples (local context-graph supervision), followed by an adaptive one-hop repair loop and RL on lower-hop items, improve accuracy on deeper multi-hop (3-5 hop) KGQA relative to KG-only (isolated-triple) supervision, and how much of the gain is attributable to context, to repair, and to RL respectively?
input.expected_contribution: A controlled, ablated characterization of how much multi-hop KGQA performance is attributable to (i) passage-local context subgraphs attached to supervision, (ii) iterative one-hop repair/cleaning, and (iii) RL fine-tuning on lower-hop items; plus evidence on whether lower-hop RL transfers to deeper hop depths. The contribution is a mechanism decomposition of an existing recipe rather than a new architecture; see novelty uncertainty (arxiv:2609.12230 appears to already report the combined recipe).
assumptions: Assumption 1 (backbone): a single open-weight ~14B instruction-tuned LLM is used throughout; architecture is not a variable. [assumption: consistent with closest retrieved work arxiv:2609.12230 naming Qwen3-14B]

Assumption 2 (data source): supervision triples and their supporting context are derived from the same source text chunk, so the context graph is passage-local rather than globally retrieved. [assumption: stated in the raw idea; matches arxiv:2609.12230]
Assumption 3 (budget control): all supervision regimes are compared at matched number of training examples and matched gradient steps; otherwise extra context tokens are a confounder.
Assumption 4 (lower-hop definition): 'lower-hop' means 1-hop and 2-hop QA items, and 'deeper' means 3-5 hop items. [assumption: not stated in the idea]
Assumption 5 (metric): primary metric is answer accuracy/exact-match, reported separately per hop depth, with the one-hop retained validation set used as a factual-foundation check.
Assumption 6 (RL algorithm): a policy-gradient-style RL fine-tuning method with a task reward (answer correctness) is used; the specific algorithm is not fixed by the idea. [unresolved]

potential_risks: The combined recipe is already published (arxiv:2609.12230), so the original idea risks being a replication rather than a novel contribution.
Context augmentation is confounded with extra supervision tokens / larger effective training signal; a matched-token or matched-example control is needed.
Repair may inflate accuracy on the retained one-hop validation set by construction (test-set cleaning / selection), so 100% one-hop accuracy is not evidence of genuine factual grounding.
Lower-hop RL gains may not transfer to unseen deeper-hop queries; gains may be explained by SFT alone or by benchmark-specific artifacts.
Domain-specific disease KGs give small evaluation sets, limiting statistical power on 3-5-hop queries.
LLM-judge-based failure detection introduces judge noise and possible self-consistency bias.

Without a matched-token/matched-example control (e.g., padding KG-only instances with unrelated or random triples from other passages), a CG-over-KG accuracy gap cannot be attributed to passage-local context specifically. This is the core mechanism claim, so it is the experiment that would most sharply distinguish a real effect from a training-signal-size artifact.

Retained sets are cleaned using information from the repair loop, so near-perfect one-hop accuracy may reflect selection on the evaluation set rather than genuine factual grounding, and the deeper-hop sets may be small. Whether the effect holds on standard benchmarks (e.g., WebQSP, ComplexWebQuestions, MetaQA) and under a held-out, non-retained split is the main external-validity question.

Motivated by these findings, we use lower-hop RL to optimize for both answer correctness and KG-path alignment, and then evaluate whether this improves generalization to harder 3-hop, 4-hop, and 5-hop question-answering.

evidence.quote: Second, we introduce an LLM-judged adaptive repair stage inspired by skill-targeted adaptive training (STAT) [23]. This stage checks whether the initial SFT models still contain unresolved one-hop missing knowledge and applies targeted adaptive repair before employing reinforcement learning (RL).

We introduce an LLM-judged, history-aware adaptive repair pipeline that improves the one-hop SFT foundation through continual targeted repair while removing or quarantining problematic noisy triples, ultimately reaching perfect accuracy on the cleaned retained validation set before employing RL.
